claim: Patch clamping technique, when used to probe for synaptic connections, is manually laborious and time-consuming.
source: The patch clamping technique, when used to probe for synaptic connections, is manually laborious and time-consuming.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the limitations of the patch clamping technique.

claim: The patch-walking approach involves cleaning just one pipette and reusing it to obtain another recording while maintaining the others.
source: instead of retracting all patch clamping electrodes after each recording attempt, we cleaned just one of them and reused it to obtain another recording while maintaining the others.
evidence: This describes the methodological approach developed in this study.

claim: With one new patch clamp recording attempt using patch-walking, many new connections can be probed.
source: With one new patch clamp recording attempt, many new connections can be probed.
evidence: This is a theoretical claim about the efficiency of the patch-walking method, supported by the mathematical modeling and experimental results.

claim: 136 patch clamp attempts were performed for two pipettes.
source: We performed 136 patch clamp attempts for two pipettes
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental data.

claim: 71 successful whole cell recordings were achieved out of 136 attempts, representing a 52.2% success rate.
source: achieving 71 successful whole cell recordings (52.2%).
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental results with calculated success rate.

claim: 29 pairs (58 bidirectional probed connections) were tested with an average intersomatic distance of 91 μm.
source: Of these, we probed 29 pairs (i.e. 58 bidirectional probed connections) averaging 91 μm intersomatic distance
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental measurements.

claim: Three synaptic connections were found among the 29 pairs tested.
source: finding three connections.
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental findings.

source: These connections, or synapses, transmit information and measuring their strength, direction, and other properties is essential to unraveling how the brain works.
evidence: This is stated as established scientific understanding about the importance of synaptic measurements.

claim: Patch clamp recording remains the gold-standard technique for high-fidelity electrophysiological measurements for studying individual neurons and their synaptic connections in the living brain.
source: Patch clamp recording remains the gold-standard technique for high-fidelity electrophysiological measurements for studying individual neurons and their synaptic connections in the living brain (Sakmann and Neher, 1984; Stuart et al., 1993; Markram et al., 1997).

claim: Patch clamp has sub-threshold resolution and millisecond precision.
source: Patch clamp, with sub-threshold resolution and millisecond precision
evidence: This is stated as an established characteristic of the patch clamp technique.

source: has enabled studies ranging from mapping the healthy rodent brain to characterizing the behavior of single cells in neurodegenerative diseases (van den Hurk et al., 2018; Castañeda-Castellanos et al., 2006; Wang et al., 2015).

source: Whole cell patch clamp recordings require forming an electrical connection between the recording electrode and the membrane of an individual neuron.

source: This electrical connection requires a high resistance seal between the neuron's membrane and a clean microelectrode pipette.

source: Detaching the pipette from this seal leaves behind residual membrane material that inhibits the formation of a new connection with another neuron.

claim: Each pipette must be cleaned or replaced after each recording.
source: Thus, each pipette must be cleaned or replaced after each recording.

claim: Skill is needed to avoid neighboring cells and account for tissue deformation when studying cells in intact tissue such as brain slices.
source: When studying cells in intact tissue such as brain slices, skill is needed to avoid neighboring cells and account for tissue deformation.

claim: Whole cell success rates are highly variable, typically ranging from 30% to 90% of attempts resulting in successful patch clamp recordings, even for experienced users.
